question: Why did the authors choose a melt-diffusion step of more than 20 hours to infiltrate the sulfur, and at what temperature was it run?
rendered: The authors did not choose a melt-diffusion step of more than 20 hours to infiltrate the sulfur. In fact, they mention that other methods traditionally employ long (>20 h) melt techniques to ensure pore infiltration or use high temperature (>300 °C) loadings for depolymerization of sulfur vapor. However, they used a low-temperature (175 °C) isothermal vapor phase process lasting 1 h to infiltrate the sulfur into the micropores of the carbon spheres.
